questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to drive around a train.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stare straight in front of their motorcycle.
Be unwilling to move to avoid a potential hazard.
Scan their path of travel, looking at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan their path of travel, looking at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead of their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds to spot hazards early. This gives you time to react before you reach the hazard.

questions.question: Usually a good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Get off the roadway.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. If you speed up, they may just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: If possible, do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What can remove alcohol from a person's system?

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol from your body. Nothing else can speed up this process.

questions.question: Which of the following is not recommended as protective apparel for motorcycle users?

options.text: Long pants
Gloves
A baseball cap

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding a motorcycle. Good choices include long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots that cover your ankles, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible.

questions.question: To minimize the potential for fatigue, you should:

options.text: Turn on the radio.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Drink caffeine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take breaks often during long rides to reduce fatigue. Caffeine may help at first, but you will crash hard when it wears off, making you more tired. Dress warmly and use a windshield to protect yourself from the elements.

questions.question: When wearing a helmet at the time of a crash, a rider is:

options.text: Less likely to survive than a person who is not wearing helmet.
Just as likely to survive as a person not wearing a helmet.
More likely to survive than a person not wearing helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than a person not wearing helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders with helmets, no matter what speed they are traveling.

questions.question: A good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Encourage the tailgater to pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage the tailgater to pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: If you can do so safely, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: Which of the following materials provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Fleece
Leather
Denim

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front brake first.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: The best way to stop quickly is to apply steady pressure to both brakes at the same time. Do not lock the brakes.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you wear?

options.text: You do not need bright clothing during the day.
You should wear bright clothing during the day.
You should wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should wear bright clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright clothing while riding to make yourself easier to see.

questions.question: How do reflective, bright helmets and clothing help you?

options.text: They should only be worn when riding at night.
They help other riders see you better.
They do not make riding safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help other riders see you better.
questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing helps other road users see you better.

questions.question: What should NOT be checked before riding?

options.text: Tires
Turn signals
Paint

questions.correctAnswerText: Paint
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, frame, and stands. Paint inspection is not necessary.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
Lanes shift.
Yield to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: When looking around your motorcycle, what should you look for?

options.text: Escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
Ways to travel faster than other vehicles.
Pedestrians to stare at.

questions.correctAnswerText: Escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
questions.explanation: Look for escape routes at intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.

questions.question: How should you load saddlebags?

options.text: Load them evenly on both sides.
Put more weight on one side.
Put all weight into one saddlebag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load them evenly on both sides.
questions.explanation: Both saddlebags should have about the same weight. Uneven weight causes the motorcycle to lean to one side.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same place as on your motorcycle.
Take it right out on the highway.
Practice in a safe area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice in a safe area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Learn where all the controls are on a borrowed motorcycle. Ride it in a safe area before taking it on the road.

questions.question: What kind of footwear should a rider wear?

options.text: Shoes that end below the ankles.
Shoes that cover the ankles.
Soft, flexible shoes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that cover the ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Can one alcoholic drink affect your ability to ride?

options.text: No, one drink will not lead to a DUI conviction.
No, one drink will never affect your riding.
Yes, one drink can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, one drink can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Impairment starts with the first drink. You can be convicted of impaired riding even if you are below the legal alcohol limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear side vision, fasten securely, let air through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: To reduce collision risk, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Ride very slowly.
Ride down the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep plenty of space between your motorcycle and other vehicles to avoid crashes. Maintain this safe distance when following other vehicles, being followed, passing, being passed, or sharing a lane.

questions.question: What should matter most when buying a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: Appearance
Protection
Price

questions.correctAnswerText: Protection
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important factor when choosing a helmet. Pick a helmet that fastens securely, fits properly, and meets DOT safety standards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction machinery, or horse-drawn carts.
